## Trial `mariadb-galera-ubuntu24__DLD8EdH`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence: a healthy three-member cluster, bidirectional multi-primary replication through every member, continued operation during a bounded single-member outage, and automatic state transfer and full recovery when that member returned.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.960 | 0.990 | 60/0 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Configure node1, node2, and node3 as one healthy three-member MariaDB Galera cluster.
  - **Why:** All three nodes finish active and enabled, report distinct node identities, the same cluster UUID and membership, cluster size 3, Primary/Connected/Ready status, and Synced local state.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-7bbdfde8b21f4501`, `cmd-5e61f525aec44b37`, `cmd-c8fd00e2f7564413`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Writes submitted through any member are replicated and available from the other members.
  - **Why:** TCP writes were successfully made through each node's managed IP. Each member subsequently read all three writes with identical row totals while the cluster remained healthy.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4057e3773eff48be`, `cmd-ba70d4735b6e4baa`, `cmd-d85a26aa3e554027`, `cmd-2443406baa284ee6`, `cmd-6cd9a2e1d9324303`, `cmd-197badbd1e4c458d`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Remain available with one member unavailable and automatically resynchronize that member when it returns.
  - **Why:** A healthy size-3 baseline was observed before node3 was stopped and its listeners disappeared. Node1 and node2 remained Primary, Ready, and writable at size 2, exchanging outage-period writes. Starting node3 normally triggered state transfer and completed IST, restored a Synced size-3 cluster, and recovered the outage-period rows; a subsequent node3 write replicated to all members.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-641b8322334043e3`, `cmd-572895267b414074`, `cmd-e6d52cd8bd1447ae`, `cmd-68cc6a24650b40eb`, `cmd-3f5df8cf49604f42`, `cmd-ccc2957e9e1f4855`, `cmd-0da2ae98a8cb45b4`, `cmd-f8e3d7e3984449f6`, `cmd-354da5eca9cc4a0a`, `cmd-6df279dbec874301`, `cmd-2bb818b523514405`, `cmd-b1ea5c67bf8f417d`, `cmd-7aad9cddfd7a4cec`, `cmd-44f0b69bf15f47ec`, `cmd-a2034e3f0a1d4f61`, `cmd-2e9b28df7f564161`

## Trial `mariadb-galera-ubuntu24__FqRAWZq`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All material outcomes are satisfied. Direct observations demonstrate a healthy three-member cluster, replication of writes submitted through every member, continued writable service during a bounded node3 outage, automatic catch-up on return, and a fully healthy recovered state.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.940 | 0.990 | 60/0 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **R1 — Satisfied:** Configure node1, node2, and node3 as one healthy three-member MariaDB Galera cluster.
  - **Why:** All nodes have the same three-address cluster configuration with unique identities. Final observations show active and enabled MariaDB services, Primary/Synced/Ready state, cluster size 3, and all three incoming member addresses.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-784ebcefb83148cf`, `cmd-06c1fe50885d4be5`, `cmd-7524986822b2435d`, `cmd-ed93d0221ff04c1d`, `cmd-4424e2355954457b`, `cmd-de58851a365a4100`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** Make writes submitted through any member available from the other members.
  - **Why:** Writes were committed independently through node1, node2, and node3. Direct final reads from every member returned all six markers, including every initial per-member write and the post-rejoin node3 write, with the same commit position.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-c14bcc16825640e6`, `cmd-e7a3547c288b428a`, `cmd-bfde44f55b4844e8`, `cmd-a74a65269ee04152`, `cmd-ed93d0221ff04c1d`, `cmd-4424e2355954457b`, `cmd-de58851a365a4100`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Keep the database available and writable while one member is unavailable.
  - **Why:** A healthy three-member baseline was observed before node3 was stopped. With node3 confirmed inactive and without database or Galera listeners, node1 and node2 remained Primary, Synced, and Ready at size 2; both accepted writes, and each survivor read both outage writes.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-9c1853eb6ffe457f`, `cmd-985edfeec2614f2d`, `cmd-7e7af1cfeae44d72`, `cmd-8b1149d5aa474c1b`, `cmd-60543bfe071d4779`, `cmd-3a447fbb33d2494e`, `cmd-4498844db1974696`, `cmd-77295223c9284522`, `cmd-0fe8df8b26d247fc`, `cmd-6614053d372245df`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** Automatically resynchronize the unavailable member when it returns.
  - **Why:** An ordinary service start returned node3. Its journal directly records receipt and application of four missing writesets by IST, transition to Synced, and readiness. Subsequent observations show all three members restored to size 3 with identical data and commit position; node3 also accepted a new write that replicated to node1 and node2.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0236082532e74b6c`, `cmd-1a6292b9d59144e8`, `cmd-e78749b152dc4e48`, `cmd-4e15947b06324a26`, `cmd-a74a65269ee04152`, `cmd-ed93d0221ff04c1d`, `cmd-4424e2355954457b`, `cmd-de58851a365a4100`
